false_text: | `chartsearchai.drugSafety.warnOnInteractions` | `true` | Flag a drug in play — asked about in the question, or named by the answer on its own authority — that interacts with one of the patient's active orders, by dataset rule, shared ATC subgroup (duplicate therapy), or shared curated cross-reactivity group (additive / duplicate-class therapy across branches); most specific match wins. An active order that is the drug in play raises nothing — restating existing therapy is not a duplicate — and so does an order whose own recorded name names the drug in play, where the reference data cannot name one of that order's ATC codes — a fixed-dose combination mapped to a combination code the dataset does not carry. Decided per co-medication by substance identity **as well as** by a shared ATC code, so a *second* order in the same class still reports ([#185](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/185)). Where **two or more** of the patient's active orders carry the drug in play — two combinations both containing it — one more chip says so and names them, *"X is already in active orders A and B — possible duplicate therapy"*; which orders count is decided on each order's displayed name, so an order whose display does not name the drug — a brand the reference data files under several substances, or an order known only by its codes — is not counted ([#477](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/477)). On a question that asks to be screened and names no drug, two or more of her orders carrying the same substances raise one chip per set of orders, *"X and Y are in active orders A and B — possible duplicate therapy"*, judged the same way, on names alone — so a cream and a tablet of one substance count, unlike the shared-class chip, which [#234](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/234) narrows by site; it is about her current therapy and is not raised on any other question. An order the concept dictionary mapped to **no** ATC code is reached by name through the reference data instead ([#228](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/228)), and is then compared on the codes that dataset files its substance under — every route it is marketed as. Where the order records where the drug is **applied** — its route concept, or its drug's dose form, read across *every* name those concepts publish rather than only the one the locale elects, since a dictionary can prefer `In both eyes` over `Bilateral eye administration` — and that recording names a site the module can attribute, those codes are narrowed to it — to the union, where it names more than one, so a cutaneous order is no longer reported as duplicating a systemic therapy the same order *mapped* to a topical code would say nothing about ([#234](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/234)). It narrows nothing where the recorded term names no site the module can attribute, and that bar is deliberately high: a term naming a route of **entry** (`Oral`, `Rectal`, `Transdermal`, `Subcutaneous` …) refuses the whole record outright, so it declines even beside a second term that does name a site. A term naming more than one site — `Topical`, which ATC uses for the anorectum as well as the skin, and form words like `Cream`, which serve either — is not a term at all, so it names nothing while another recorded term may still narrow. Reading such a word as the skin *silences* a real claim, which is the direction this must not fail in. It also narrows nothing where the dataset files the substance under no code at the site recorded — the substance-level classification is then the only one there is — and, for several orders of one substance, it declines for all of them as soon as one is a presentation it cannot place. What that gives up: a locally applied presentation which is nonetheless systemically absorbed (ophthalmic timolol against an oral beta-blocker) loses a chip it used to raise. Both of those are pairwise, so both report most severe first, capped by `chartsearchai.drugSafety.maxPairChips`, with how many pairs were withheld and at what ratings logged. It also gates the condition-mediated finding (issues #391 and #473), which additionally needs `chartsearchai.drugSafety.derivedFindings` set to `major` and is off by default. |

false_text: **What you can put beside it, and what you cannot — and the honest answer is: less than you would like.** No prose travels with this key, and the response does not let you recover the cited record's own words for a given index. Two things stand in the way, both measured rather than assumed. A `safety_finding`'s `resourceUuid` is `"<type>:<drug>"` and names the SUBJECT drug only, so one drug screened against several active orders produces several records — several citation indexes — sharing one `resourceUuid`, and several `safetyWarnings[]` chips sharing one `(type, drug)`. The chips carrying that pair are therefore a candidate SET, not a match: render them together or render none, because picking one arbitrarily is how a client ends up showing a different partner's mechanism beside the very citation it is flagging. And even for a single-candidate case the chip's `detail` is only the record's **mechanism** half — the record the check compares against also carries the `Safety finding — <drug>: ` prefix and the clauses `renderFinding` appends — the strength call, the chart-order bridges, the provenance note — inside which a divergence can perfectly well fall. Of those the strength call and the prefix appear on no wire key at all; two are exceptions, and neither is the counterpart it looks like. The chart-order clause, because what is published is its ITEMS, as the structured [`chartOrderBridges`](#search) array on the chip, and not the clause TEXT this check compares against. Its own invariant lead is on no key either, and on an install that sets [`chartsearchai.drugSafety.citeOrderRecords`](#drug-reference--safety-optional-off-by-default) a rendered item also carries the citation number of the chart record its order is wherever the module could resolve one ([#379](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/379)), which the structured array does not. And the provenance note, because what is published is the ANSWER it is appended off — the chip's own [`restsOnAnUncorroboratedChartMatch`](#search) boolean ([#374](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-chartsearchai/issues/374)) — and again not the clause text. For a `drug_reference` citation there is no counterpart at all: that record's text is prompt-facing and names this patient's recorded allergens and conditions, and it is not published. So treat this key as a flag on a rendering, not as a pointer to a correction.

false_text: <description>Most interaction chips one question may raise from a PAIRWISE check — the drugs the question itself names checked against each other, or (for a question that names no drug and asks to be screened) the patient's active orders checked against each other. Both are quadratic in a list this module does not choose: pairs grow as N²/2, so 16 named drugs is 120 candidate pairs and 10 active orders is 45. Every chip is also injected into the prompt as a citable finding, so an uncapped check both buries the clinician and expands the context window without bound (measured: 72 chips carrying 42,708 characters from one 16-drug question). THE TRADE-OFF IS REAL AND IT IS YOURS TO MAKE: raising this shows more pairs and costs prompt space and clinician attention; leaving it low withholds pairs, and on a long medication list some of those withheld pairs are rated Major (measured on the full DDInter data, a 16-drug question: 10 of 72 pairs shown, [Major ×13, Moderate ×40, Minor ×9] withheld — thirteen withheld Majors). What is dropped is always the least severe — candidates are sorted most-severe-first before the cut — and a WARN log line reports how many pairs were withheld and at what ratings. It does not name them: in the active-order screen both sides of a pair are the patient's own prescriptions, so naming them wrote her medication list to the server log (issue #439). The COUNTS also reach the response itself, as an interactionPairs object stating how many above-floor pairs were found beside how many were reported, so a client can say "10 of 18 shown" and a clinician can tell a bounded list from a complete one. What stays in the log alone is the withheld pairs' ratings (how many went follows from interactionPairs), because putting the withheld pairs on the wire would be the unbounded expansion this cap exists to prevent. To see which pairs went, raise this property and ask again — which REPRODUCES the screen rather than recovering it: for a request already served, which pairs were withheld is unrecoverable, and re-asking shows them only while the chart and the question still raise them. A polypharmacy review clinic may want 30 where a triage screen wants 5. Unparseable or non-positive values fall back to the default rather than disabling the cap. Both pairwise checks read this one property: their triggers are mutually exclusive, so no question is subject to both. It bounds those two and nothing else — the drug-in-play check, which screens a drug the question names against the patient's own medications, is not capped, and states an interactionPairs object of its own where neither pairwise check stated one AND the question resolved a drug it could screen, so where a screening check states nothing nothing else states the field at all.
